title: Multimodal embeddings
summary: A multimodal embedding model puts text and images into one vector space, so a text query can retrieve images and an image can retrieve look-alikes. You get similarity but no explanation or citation text.
useIf: Users search by example image, or you need look-alike retrieval without an LLM call per image at index time.
avoidIf: Answers need citable text or reasons. Verbalizing the image into text is the better path.

explain.md: A **multimodal embedding** model maps images and text into the same vector space. A text query and a matching photo land close together, and two similar photos land close to each other. Each item gets one vector, scored by cosine similarity. That makes cross-modal search cheap: no LLM at index time, and image-to-vector queries work. The cost is that a vector explains nothing, so you cannot show why a result matched or quote it as a citation [[r12]].

At query time you embed the query with the same model and take the nearest neighbours: a text query finds images and an image query finds look-alikes. Use one model version per corpus. Single-vector models keep one vector per item. Multi-vector output, which `jina-embeddings-v4` also offers, keeps many vectors per item and trades storage for finer matching [[r23]].

explain.title: One space for text and images
explain.alt: Images are embedded at index time. Text or image queries are embedded with the same model and matched by nearest neighbour search.

explain.title: Index size
explain.expr: bytes = items x dimensions x bytes_per_value
explain.example: 10 million images at 1,024 dimensions is 10M x 1,024 x 4 = **40.96 GB**. At 512 dimensions it is **20.48 GB**. Compare a multi-vector page index in the page-image topic.

explain.title: Do not mix versions or compare raw scores
explain.md: Vectors from different models are not comparable, and Azure Vision relevance scores do not compare across queries. Re-embed the whole corpus when you change model version, and rank within each query [[r13]].

pitfalls.symptom: Similarity scores look arbitrary across queries
pitfalls.cause: Azure Vision relevance scores do not compare across queries
pitfalls.fix: Use per-query ranks and thresholds tuned on a golden set.

pitfalls.symptom: Results degrade after a model upgrade
pitfalls.cause: New and old vectors were mixed in one index, and they are not comparable
pitfalls.fix: Re-embed into a new index and switch an alias.

pitfalls.symptom: Image search finds look-alikes but cannot say why
pitfalls.cause: Embeddings carry no explanation or citation text
pitfalls.fix: Add a verbalization path for the same corpus.

scenarios.title: Find products from a photo
scenarios.situation: A marketplace lets shoppers upload a photo to find similar items. The catalogue has 20 million images. Latency is tight and nobody needs a written reason.
unknowns: Which languages are in text queries?
scenarios.question: How do you index?

options.name: Embed images with a multimodal embedding model and search by vector
options.why: Image-to-vector queries and look-alike search are the use case, and no LLM runs at index time [[r12]].

options.name: Caption every image and search the text
options.why: Captions lose visual nuance, make photo queries awkward and cost one LLM call per image.
options.tradeoff: Right when users need text results and citations.

options.name: Page-image multi-vector retrieval
options.tradeoff: Far larger index and designed for documents, not product photos.

flips.then: Add a text field and hybrid search.
Add captions or attributes for citation.

scenarios.title: Model version upgrade
scenarios.situation: A live index of 50 million images uses an older embedding model version. The team wants the multilingual version, and the index serves traffic daily.
constraints: Vectors from different models are not comparable
unknowns: Can traffic tolerate a staged cutover?
scenarios.question: How do you migrate?

options.name: Build a new index with the new model, then switch traffic by alias
options.why: Old and new vectors cannot be compared, so the whole corpus must be re-embedded, and a swap avoids mixed results [[r13]].
options.tradeoff: Temporary double storage and embedding cost.

options.name: Embed new images with the new model into the old index
options.why: It mixes incomparable vectors and corrupts ranking.

options.name: Embed queries with the new model against the old index
options.why: Query and index vectors come from different spaces.
options.tradeoff: Works only if both use the same model version.

flips.then: A short maintenance window with an in-place rebuild is fine.
Run both indexes in parallel on a golden set before the switch.

scenarios.takeaway: A model change is an index rebuild.

scenarios.title: Shrinking a 100 million item index
scenarios.situation: A media archive embeds 100 million items with `embed-v4.0` at the default 1536 dimensions. Storage cost is too high.
scenarios.question: What do you do first?

options.name: Test 512 and 1024 on a golden set and choose the smallest that meets recall
options.why: 100M x 1,536 x 4 B is about 614 GB, against about 205 GB at 512, so measurement can cut cost by two thirds.
options.tradeoff: You need a golden set and a re-embed.

options.name: Keep 1536 and buy more storage
options.tradeoff: Pays about 3 times the storage for possibly unneeded precision.

options.name: Choose 256 dimensions without testing
options.why: Recall may fall below target and you only find out in production.
options.tradeoff: Fine if a test shows it meets the target.

flips.then: Stay at a higher size and look at other compression.

scenarios.takeaway: Measure recall by dimension before paying for storage.

quiz.q: How many gigabytes does an index of 2 million 1,024-dimension float32 vectors need (decimal GB, vectors only)?
After upgrading the embedding model, new images rank oddly against old ones. Why?
options: Vectors from different models are not comparable
Cosine similarity stops working above 1,000 items
The index ran out of dimensions
quiz.explain: The docs warn that vectors from different models are not comparable, so rebuild the index. Cosine works at any size, cross-modal search is the point, and dimensions are a model property.

quiz.q: Which are documented properties of Azure Vision multimodal embeddings?
quiz.explain: Scores are not comparable across queries, so the third option is false.

flashcards.front: What is the main strength and limit of single-vector multimodal embeddings?
flashcards.back: Strength: text-to-image and image-to-image search with no LLM at index time. Limit: no explanation or citation text for a match.

flashcards.front: What are Azure Vision multimodal embedding limits?
flashcards.back: 1,024 dimensions, image under 20 MB and 10 x 10 to 16,000 x 16,000 px, text 1 to 70 words. Scores are not comparable across queries or model versions.
256, 512, 1024 or 1536 (default), with 128k context and text, images and mixed PDFs. `embed-v5.0-pro` and `-fast` offer up to 2048.
